text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Hope rises of a quick ending to truckers conflict, as agreement reached on early retirement at 57-1/2 years of age, or 55 for drivers who have been working for 25 years. Estimated cost for the state is 400 million francs. Issues of pay rises and payment of all working time remain to be settled, 250 road blockades remain. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)
-- UAP vice-chairman Didier Pfeiffer named new GAN chairman, may consider naming Erap chairman Philippe Pontet to replace CIC chairman Bernard Yoncourt.
(Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation)
-- Eurotunnel expects total cost of last week's fire around one billion francs, under the ceiling fixed by insurers, says passenger traffic to resume next week.
-- Schneider, launches a management buy-out for its construction subsidiary Spie Batignolles, part of which it plans to sell to Britain's Amec.
-- EU Committee to make statements on the French government's Thomson privatisation, on December 4 on competition, and December 18 for recapitalisation.
-- Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing at the National Assembly calls for a seven franc-euro parity.
-- Industry heads consider increasing production in the next quarter, notably in consumer goods and agri-food products, national statistics office INSEE survey shows.
-- LVMH LVMH.PA luxury goods group buys Chateau d'Yquem, a prestigious Sauternes wine producer, for an estimated one billion francs.
-- A planned merger of Alcatel Alsthom and nuclear plant maker Framatome may jeopardise Framatome's partnership with Germany's Siemens SIEG.F on nuclear reactors.
